meta.storyTitle: Recover run-file guards whose recorded owner is conclusively dead instead of withholding daemon restart

override.reason: Daemon design review unavailable: attempt 1 rejected standalone LLD provenance at admission (no Epic/ISSUE link), attempt 2 failed with a daemon-side busy error (known broken review path since 2026-11-01). Controller self-review completed with fresh reads verifying all citations (c1-c6, c8) and the fail-closed guarantees; user approved in-chat.

alternativesConsidered.name: Reclaim inside the shared acquireRunFileGuard (dead-owner verdict + rename-to-quarantine + retry)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The EEXIST branch itself decides dead vs live and self-heals; all guard consumers inherit it for free.
alternativesConsidered.approach: On EEXIST inside acquireRunFileGuard (src/shared/daemon-run-files.ts:64-92), before throwing runFileGuardConflict: read the existing owner.json, compute the liveness verdict with processIdentityState (src/shared/daemon-process.ts:77-80) plus a boot-id comparison. If conclusively dead - 'gone', or the recorded boot-id differs from the current boot (a previous-boot record is dead even when its PID reads 'replaced') - rename the stale guard directory to a quarantine name (timestamp + recorded nonce, matching the manual-quarantine convention) and retry the mkdir once. Rename+mkdir is atomic against competing starters (kernel-serialized on the same parent). Missing/corrupt/unreadable owner.json keeps the existing fail-closed throw. Recovery logged (prior owner identity + quarantine path) so the owner record survives as evidence. No new exports; every consumer - startup lease, supervisor borrow, legacy cutover, vault guard - inherits it. borrowRunFileGuard and removeOwnedRunFile untouched.
pros: Smallest surface that fully meets the Story: one module, one branch
Fixes every consumer path at once - all four funnel through acquireRunFileGuard
Reuses the existing PID-reuse-safe identity machinery; no new identity code
Prior owner.json preserved by rename, keeping the evidence trail
Competing starters stay serialized; a live concurrent starter can never lose its guard
cons: acquireRunFileGuard grows from a pure mkdir-or-throw primitive to one with a recovery side effect - the 'crash mid-publication is deliberately fail-closed' comment must be narrowed to the unverifiable-owner case
the retry must not mask a live owner (retry happens only after a successful rename, so a live owner's guard is never renamed)

alternativesConsidered.name: Recovery at the daemon ownership wrapper (DaemonRunFileOwnership.lease)
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep the shared primitive pure; make the daemon's ownership wrapper the recovery policy owner.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep acquireRunFileGuard fail-closed and instead teach DaemonRunFileOwnership.lease (src/daemon/run-file-ownership.ts:51-62) to pre-recover: catch runFileGuardConflict, run the same dead-owner verdict, quarantine-and-retry, then re-acquire. The shared primitive stays a pure mkdir-mutex; recovery is a policy of the daemon's ownership wrapper where isAlreadyRunning (:117-135) already implements the analogous stale pid-file policy.
pros: The shared module's fail-closed contract and documented crash-mid-publication invariant stay byte-identical
Recovery lives beside isAlreadyRunning, the existing staleness-recovery precedent
Blast radius confined to the daemon startup path this Issue was reproduced against
cons: The keystore vault guard (src/shared/keystore.ts:96-100) and legacy cutover (src/daemon/legacy-daemon-cutover.ts:29-98) do NOT go through DaemonRunFileOwnership, so the offline maintenance tool keeps the original orphan failure - the fix is only half-delivered
Verdict + quarantine + retry logic duplicated if any second consumer needs it; two recovery policies to keep in sync
runFileGuardConflict must carry the recorded owner details to the wrapper so the verdict can be recomputed
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Leaves vault guard and cutover unfixed; violates shared-module placement.

alternativesConsidered.name: Separate shared recovery module consumed by acquireRunFileGuard
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Factor verdict + quarantine + retry into its own exported unit that the guard calls on conflict.
alternativesConsidered.approach: New module exporting reclaimIfConclusivelyDead(path, identityReader) returning 'reclaimed' | 'unverifiable' | 'alive', implementing verdict + rename + log; acquireRunFileGuard calls it on EEXIST and throws runFileGuardConflict unless it reports 'reclaimed'. The decision table gets its own focused test file; the guard module keeps only the retry wiring.
pros: The verdict table (gone / boot-mismatch / replaced / same / unreadable) is testable in isolation from the mkdir mechanics
Guard module stays small; recovery policy is deletable without touching the mutex
Natural seam if a future CLI wants an operator 'why was my start withheld' probe
cons: A module boundary nobody asked for: one caller, one use
Splits the guard's failure handling across two files
Larger import/dependency footprint for no additional reuse today
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: All constraints met but adds a one-caller module boundary.

alternativesConsidered.name: Reclaim (a1) plus separately close the shutdown-deadline orphan window
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Also change the fail-closed cleanup so it never re-creates the guard the watchdog's SIGKILL can orphan.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The dead-owner reclaim of a1 AND additionally stop the most common orphan at its source: change clearRunFiles (src/daemon/run-file-ownership.ts:106-114) so shutdown cleanup removes daemon.pid/daemon.sock without re-creating the guard (or reorder the watchdog arming so it cannot kill inside the guard window), removing the shutdown-deadline race observed at 2026-11-13 05:01.
pros: Eliminates the most frequently observed orphan at its cause rather than healing it afterward
Would reduce recovery-path log noise to genuinely external kills only
cons: Out of scope: the Issue's recorded user decision is that with dead-owner reclaim in place the known orphan windows become benign and are NOT separately fixed
Touches the fail-closed shutdown path (src/daemon/shutdown.ts:164-170) and the watchdog contract - the most safety-critical code in the daemon
Two independent behavior changes in one Story; each deserves its own ledger entry if ever pursued
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Contradicts the ISSUE's scope decision; touches fail-closed shutdown code.

api.name: acquireRunFileGuard

parameters.name: read
parameters.purpose: injected ProcessIdentityReader for verdicts and tests

postconditions: On success the guard directory holds a fresh owner.json naming the caller
On reclaim the stale guard persists as a quarantine sibling with owner.json intact
On withhold the guard directory is byte-identical to before the call
preconditions: The parent of `path` exists and is writable
On EEXIST the recorded owner identity is readable and a verdict is computable

returns.meaning: the acquired guard; the EEXIST branch reclaims conclusively-dead occupants and retries the mkdir once

api.signature: acquireRunFileGuard(path: string, owner?: ProcessIdentity, read?: ProcessIdentityReader): RunFileGuard

errorCases.response: Recompute conflict vs new occupant; throw
Suffix retry; persistent failure rethrows, guard untouched

invariantsToPreserve.text: A live owner ('same') is never reclaimed.
A missing or unreadable owner record is never treated as dead.
Rename-then-mkdir preserves the atomic arbitration between starters.
The child never removes a supervisor-owned guard; borrowRunFileGuard untouched.
Nothing is recursively deleted; the reclaim renames the directory whole.
The reclaim lives in shared acquireRunFileGuard; vault guard and cutover inherit it.

boundary.internal: Recover run-file guards whose recorded owner is conclusively dead instead of withholding daemon restart

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature - no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

migration.backwardCompat: Additive: call sites, conflict message and owner.json format unchanged; supervisor protocol untouched.

migrationSteps.action: EEXIST branch: read owner record, verdict, compare boot segments
Reclaim: quarantine rename (timestamp+nonce, suffixed), daemonLog line, one retry, recompute on retry EEXIST

migration.stateAfter: Conclusively-dead occupants reclaim: quarantine rename keeping owner.json, one daemonLog line, one mkdir retry; live/same-boot/unverifiable still throw; all consumers inherit.
migration.stateBefore: Every existing guard withholds: EEXIST throws runFileGuardConflict, verdict discarded; each orphan blocks restart until manual quarantine (six since 2026-11-02).

provingTests: int: lease over a dead-owner guard (src/daemon/__tests__/run-file-ownership.test.ts)
unit: owner.json byte-identical; nonce in quarantine name; daemonLog line by nonce
unit: retry EEXIST -> recompute conflict, throw
unit: 'same'/same-boot 'replaced'/missing or corrupt owner.json/throwing reader -> withhold
int: vault guard reclaims (src/daemon/__tests__/keystore-guard.test.ts); supervisor suites unchanged

testLevels.purpose: Decision table via injected reader over mkdtemp guards.
subjects: same / same-boot replaced / unverifiable -> conflict, nothing renamed
quarantine name = timestamp + nonce; owner.json intact; daemonLog line
